title: THIS STUFF IS MAGIC!!!👏🏾👏🏾👏🏾👏🏾👏🏾
date: Reviewed in the United States on November 12, 2024
review: I have been using this for 3 days and it WORKS! You have to follow the directions exactly. Some of the reviews are negative because people aren’t reading the directions clearly. You need to have patience. The directions say to use it every day for a week. It says NOT to use boiling water or chemicals or it will counteract and not work. You have to run the sink full of water and drain it. After the water is out you put a cup of that formula down the drain. You can’t use that sink for at least 6 hours. I do all of my drains (including the bathtubs) at night before bed. You have to do it for a week until the drain flies are all gone. Then weekly as a preventative measure. If you have a garbage disposal (we do) you have to fill the sink then run the garbage disposal. Turn off the garbage disposal. Add the formula and turn the garbage disposal back on to coat the inside.  Be patient.

title: Fly stickers ALONE were worth the purchase !!
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 18, 2024
review: I got these and put the fly stickers on all my drains.  I had been using "Green Gobbler for Fruit & Drain Flies" for about 3-4 days in my drains with NO noticeable difference in the fly population in my house!  I put these stickers on my drains and the next morning I got up and there were NO flies in my house!  But guess what? There weren't any stuck to the fly stickers either.  It's been three days with my drains plugged.  A plug in the bathroom tub, stopper pulled up in the bathroom sink, one fly sticker still stuck to one drain in my kitchen double sink and I just keep the drain stopper in the other sink so I still have a sink in the kitchen to use. Still not a single fly on the sticker, but no flies in the house either.  I wanted to see just how long I'd be 'fly free' doing this.  -So far, 3 days with NO flies AND I still haven't put the EcoStrong drain treatment in the drains! So, the drains ARE the problem.  At first I didn't think so.  I never saw a fly come out of the drains -ever! I live in a duplex and my sinks, tub and probably toilet all drain to a center drain pipe in the common wall that I and my next door neighbor share.  I'm sure she's been inundated with flies.  Those little buggers are smart!  Not one was stuck to the fly stickers but the fact that I had NO flies the next day after putting them on before going to bed and then got up to a fly free house tells me that's where they're coming from.  If I even go get a fly swatter and sit back down at my desk in front of my living room window the flys would vanish.  They KNEW I had that swatter.  They would hid behind my desk calendar or along the edge of my laptop on my desk. -anywhere they could find that I couldn't get at them, so not surprised there was none on the fly stickers.  They knew better.  They just went down the other side of the drain to my neighbors house!  If I didn't get anything but the stickers with this purchase it would have been worth the $36 to me to find this out!  I spent $250 on fly zappers, fly trap bags and other crap and NONE of it worked! -I even took clear packing tape and sealed all my windows in my house shut thinking that's where they were coming in, under the weatherstripping and was getting ready to replace all my window's weatherstripping!  Thank you EcoStrong for the stickers!! I'm gonna use the drain treatment to treat my drains. -As soon as I get another sink stopper to seal the other side of my kitchen sink so I can take the sticker off!  -And I'm gonna buy a gallon and some stickers for my next door neighbor.  With our drains being in common we're gonna have to tackle this together to get rid of these buggers.  But if she won't be diligent and do her side, I'm just gonna keep treating my side and keep my drains closed unless I'm right there running water into them. It's the only solution I can figure out, but at least, thank God! I HAVE a solution that works now!UPDATE:  I used the Eco Strong Drain treatment in all four of my house drains, kitchen sinks, bathroom sink and tub for 8 straight days before I went to bed. I put a strip of blue painters tape across my kitchen sink so I wouldn't accidently forget I treated the drains and use the sink.  I pulled up the bathroom sink stopper & put a small mixing bowl in the bathroom sink so I could wash my hands and run water from that faucet into the mixing bowl, then dumped the bowl into the toilet next to the sink and set it back in the sink for reuse.  That  little system worked pretty well for the 8 day treatment so that it wasn't much hassle not being able to use the sinks for about 10-12 hours during the night.  After 8 days I'm pretty much fly free. I bought a gallon with the stickers for my next door neighbor and gave it to her to use, since our sinks connect to the same drain pipe.  I live in a duplex and we have a common wall so our kitchens and bathrooms back up to each other and use a common drain pipe to the septic tank.  I'm not sure how faithful and diligent she's been on her side but she told me a couple days ago she only has a few flys now instead of the hoards of flys we were both dealing with so I think this stuff works.  I'm going to continue once a week treatments through fly season and keep my sink and tub stoppers in place when I'm not running water into them.  Can't think of anything else to do and the treatments drastically reduced the flys.  Wish it was a 'zero fly zone' but those little buggers are smart.  I'm looking for and closing any remaining entrances they may be getting in from. Fixing to put up a split door screen on my front door.  I think some are getting in that way.
